question: Read the following situation: An educator is starting to work on identifying numbers to develop quantification skills in preschoolers. As a first activity, she wants the boys and girls to be able to identify the number 1. Given her knowledge of the level, she knows that Vicente is an active child, who learns much better by using his body, so she will ask him to imitate a number 1. On the other hand, she also knows that Martina and Clemente have many musical skills and learn quickly through songs, so she will include some in the experience. Which pedagogical principle of Early Childhood Education is mainly highlighted in the planning of this educator?
answer_a: Empowerment
answer_b: Uniqueness
answer_c: Relationship
answer_d: Play

question: Which of the options presents an expected manifestation of cognitive development in boys and girls who are beginning the pre-operational stage?
answer_a: Use of symbolic thought
answer_b: Drawing abstract conclusions
answer_c: Application of deductive reasoning
answer_d: Interaction with the environment through experimental games

question: Consider the following situation: An early years teacher has two rows of blocks that contain the same amount, but one of the rows appears longer because the blocks are more spaced out. One of the children comes up to the teacher and says, 'Miss, this row has more blocks than the other.' According to J. Piaget's theory, what characteristic thought process is evidenced in the child's comment?
answer_a: Centration
answer_b: Syncretism
answer_c: Transduction
answer_d: Irreversibility

question: A child, walking with his father in the rain, looks up at the sky and points to the clouds saying: 'The clouds are sad, that's why they are crying.' According to Jean Piaget's cognitive theory, what characteristic of thought is reflected in the child's statement?
answer_a: Animism
answer_b: Syncretism
answer_c: Artificialism
answer_d: Phenomenism

question: Read the following definition: It is the first form of play for human beings. They are usually individual games that consist of repetitive muscular movements. What type of game does the previous definition correspond to?
answer_a: Constructive
answer_b: Symbolic
answer_c: Functional
answer_d: Parallel

question: What skills are mainly developed in children through structured play?
answer_a: The symbolization of real-life situations
answer_b: Empathy and conflict resolution
answer_c: Socializing elements of agreements and turns
answer_d: Learning of practices and roles established in social settings

question:
Read the following situation:
Patricia, an early years educator, invites five children from her class each week to lead small group work.
She tells the children that the leader will suggest a group game and encourage their peers to follow the rules of the proposed game.
According to Erikson's stages of socio-emotional development, which one is reflected in the previous learning experience?
answer_a: Initiative vs. guilt
answer_b: Trust vs. mistrust
answer_c: Industry vs. inferiority
answer_d: Autonomy vs. shame and doubt

question: In an early years group, boys and girls are chalk painting a mural in the schoolyard. Fabián tells the educator that he doesn’t want to paint because only pink chalk is left and pink is a girls' color. The educator tells him that colors are for everyone, not just for boys or girls, and he should try painting with it as artists do. In relation to identity, which aspect does the reflection initiated by the educator help develop?
answer_a: Self-esteem
answer_b: Self-concept
answer_c: Sexual identity
answer_d: Gender identity

question: Consider the following situation: An early years educator sets up a conversation activity with the children during circle time, which begins by asking them: "How do you feel today?" Each child responds and then picks one of the cards that the educator has prepared in advance, representing different expressions such as surprise, disgust, fear, anger, sadness, and joy. What learning related to identity development is promoted by the described activity?
answer_a: Express emotions
answer_b: Recognize emotions
answer_c: Manifest feelings
answer_d: Identify feelings

question: Which of the following situations shows the ability of a child in kindergarten to regulate his or her emotions and feelings?
answer_a: Juan Pablo was very eager to play an elf in the end-of-year play, but since another child already took the role, he agrees to play one of the reindeer
answer_b: Cristián discusses the differences in preferences he has with his classmates regarding the different games and sports played at school
answer_c: Paloma had many problems during the execution of a task and, in the group meeting, she explains and points out the solutions she applied
answer_d: Rafaela joins a group of classmates who collect toys to donate to a children's home

question: According to Kohlberg's theory of moral development, which of the following options corresponds to a concept of the first stage of preconventional morality?
answer_a: What is just is to follow the rule only when it benefits another
answer_b: What is just is blind obedience to the rule, avoiding punishments
answer_c: What is just is to fulfill duties that have been previously accepted before the group
answer_d: What is just is to live according to what the people close to oneself expect

question: Language is not innate, it is learned and depends on the relationships that the individual establishes with people and, in general, with the surrounding culture. Therefore, inheritance is not determinant. It develops in stages, from birth to school age. To which author does this conception of language development correspond?
answer_a: H. Maturana
answer_b: D. Ausubel
answer_c: L. Vygotsky
answer_d: J. Piaget

question: According to J. Piaget, one of the characteristics of early speech is that children overgeneralize the meanings of words. Which of the following options is an example of the characteristic indicated?
answer_a: A child says “ato” to the toy car his dad gave him. When shown another car, he says “no ato”
answer_b: A child, upon looking at a photo of himself with his mother, repeats along with her: “affectionate, beautiful, proud” and then the child adds “loving”
answer_c: A child says “tata”, pointing to the image of a gray-haired man in a magazine
answer_d: A child says “papa” every time he is given his bottle

question: In a handball class, two students fiercely contest the ball; one pushes the other to keep the ball, and the other responds with insults. The teacher calls both students to clarify what happened, and after hearing them, applies the established rule: a verbal warning to both. What conflict resolution method did the teacher apply?
answer_a: Mediation
answer_b: Negotiation
answer_c: Arbitration
answer_d: Consensual agreement

question: Read the following situation: Two children are playing and both are speaking at the same time, expressing their thoughts, although without addressing each other. According to J. Piaget, which cognitive development stage is manifested by the language presented in the above situation?
answer_a: Preoperational
answer_b: Sensorimotor
answer_c: Formal operations
answer_d: Concrete operations

question: The teacher wants to assign a reinforcement task to the 50% of the class that got the lowest scores on a test. Which of the following data allows selecting these students?
answer_a: The mode
answer_b: The mean
answer_c: The median
answer_d: The frequency

question: Read the following situation: An educator organizes an activity called 'protagonist of the day', which consists of a child, each day, sharing with their classmates their preferences, interests, and hobbies through photos, memories, toys, and anecdotes. What pedagogical principle is present in the above situation?
answer_a: Meaning
answer_b: Relationship
answer_c: Singularity
answer_d: Well-being

question:
Read the following situation:
An educator plays with playdough alongside a child in her group in the arts area. She takes a piece and divides it into two equal parts. Then she shows it to the child and says, "Are the pieces of playdough equal?" The child replies, "Yes, they are equal." Next, the educator stretches one of the pieces and asks, "Now, which piece has more playdough?" And the child says, "This one has more," pointing to the one the educator stretched.
What characteristic of preoperational thought is reflected in the above situation?
answer_a: Finalism
answer_b: Transduction
answer_c: Centration
answer_d: Artificialism

question:
Read the following text: 
Language is yet another manifestation of the human capacity for symbolization. For it to develop, maturity of mental and psychological processes is required.
Which theory of language development is related to the previous text?
answer_a: Social
answer_b: Innatist
answer_c: Cognitive
answer_d: Behaviorist

question: Read the following situation: A preschool educator proposes a role-playing game: "Lost in the Jungle." It is about some children who get lost in a jungle where there are wild animals, unexplored places, abandoned caves, and many dangers. Before starting the game, they must choose a guide to save the group. The educator then invites each child to explain why they believe they are the right one to save the group, and asks them to express their strengths and skills for this task. What aspect related to the development of identity is favored in the children with the proposed experience?
answer_a: Empathy
answer_b: Initiative
answer_c: Self-esteem
answer_d: Collaboration

question: An upper preschool educator has observed that Francisco, one of the children in the class group, is impulsive and irritable during the routine. He shouts or cries when he does not achieve what he has set out to do and takes materials from the children, ending in fights among them. When the educator asks him what is happening to him or what he feels, Francisco frowns, crosses his arms, and says nothing, refusing to speak. This situation has been repeated for several weeks since the beginning of the school year. The educator decides to work with him to strengthen his ability to recognize his emotions. Which of the following activities is most suitable to start this process?
answer_a: Tell Francisco when he is showing an adverse emotion so that he can regulate it
answer_b: Tell Francisco stories where it is explained how harmful the emotions he shows are
answer_c: Ask classmates to provide solutions to Francisco so he can control his emotions
answer_d: Provide a board where Francisco can mark the face that corresponds to the emotion he feels

question: Read the following situation: During recess for a group of preschoolers, José approaches his classmate Rocío to play, but she continues to play alone. After recess, José, upset, takes the girl's work and folders, throws them on the floor, and steps on them. Rocío cries and runs to the teacher to tell her what happened. The teacher, to resolve the conflict, approaches José, asks him to look at his classmate, and asks him how he thinks Rocío feels and what he will do to remedy the situation. The boy approaches Rocío, hugs her, and offers to pick up the folders and clean the work. Considering the situation presented, why might the strategy used by the teacher help develop cohabitation skills in José?
answer_a: Because it teaches the child to control his impulses
answer_b: Because it promotes the development of empathy towards others
answer_c: Because it teaches the child to internalize rules of conduct
answer_d: Because it allows the child to learn to show affection and care towards others

question: Read the following situation: During activity time, two children are in a dispute over using a puzzle: Josefina pushes Marcos to take the game away from him, and Marcos responds with a kick. The educator approaches to offer her help, and both, crying, try to explain what happened. The educator comforts them and then separately listens to each one's version of events. After that, she gathers them to discuss what happened and explains that they should listen to each other with respect and without violence to resolve the dispute. She asks both to express how they felt about the aggression from their peer and asks them how they think they could resolve the conflict. Josefina suggests they apologize and Marcos suggests sharing the pieces and assembling the puzzle together. Both agree to the proposed solutions and continue playing. Which peaceful conflict resolution technique does the educator's intervention in the described situation correspond to?
answer_a: Arbitration
answer_b: Mediation
answer_c: Facilitation
answer_d: Conciliation

question: Read the following situation: A preschool educator is working in the verbal language area with the following chart, which she completes with the children in her group. What metalinguistic skill is developed through the resource used in this activity?
answer_a: Semantic awareness
answer_b: Phonological awareness
answer_c: Pragmatic awareness
answer_d: Morphosyntactic awareness

question: In which of the following options is the schematic stage of children's drawing characterized?
answer_a: There is a more defined concept of shape, object-color relationship, and actions are included in the drawings
answer_b: The human figure appears in the shape of a tadpole, details begin to be included, and there is juxtaposition
answer_c: There is a main figure and the space is everything that surrounds this figure, other elements float around it
answer_d: The strokes are controlled, there is representational intent, but little object-color relationship

question:
Read the following situation: 
An educator aims to enhance artistic expression through the development of kinesthetic skills of the children in her preschool group.
Which of the following activities is the most appropriate to achieve her goal?
answer_a: Painting a picture while observing different landscapes of nature
answer_b: Singing different songs while marking the rhythm with percussion instruments
answer_c: Dancing to the rhythm of the music while regulating movements and breathing
answer_d: Assembling a collage using papers of different colors, thicknesses, and textures

question: A teacher of a 4th grade class who is working with her students on children's rights presents the following situation: "Anita suffered a severe blow to the head when she fell from the slide while playing with her classmates in the school yard. After the accident, Anita was quickly taken by her teacher to the emergency service, where she received the required attention." Then, the teacher asks the students to recognize the right that Anita is exercising in the described situation and finally, to present another situation in which that same right would be asserted. Which of the following indicators is relevant to assess the students' learning in the last activity proposed by the teacher?
answer_a: They identify the main rights of children
answer_b: They illustrate rights they exercise in their daily lives with concrete examples
answer_c: They formulate opinions about the importance of exercising and protecting their rights
answer_d: They recognize instances where children's rights are violated

question: An educator plans an activity in which the boys and girls of her group will receive a visit from a 1st Grade class from the school. When they arrive, each preschool child will sit next to a 1st Grade child, and they will be encouraged to get to know each other through conversation. Afterwards, they will make a drawing together and go out to the yard to share games. Finally, they will discuss in a large group the experience they had together. Which of the following pedagogical principles is mainly promoted with this learning experience?
answer_a: Unity
answer_b: Relationship
answer_c: Meaning
answer_d: Empowerment

question: The educator, in a constant period of group meeting, invites the boys and girls to remember an achievement of theirs in recent times. To exemplify the exercise, she tells them that she is taking yoga classes and that with great effort she managed to do the lion pose. A girl says she managed to jump with both feet together, a boy points out that he managed to close one eye. In the described situation, which emotional component of autonomy is being promoted?
answer_a: Empathy
answer_b: Confidence
answer_c: Self-regulation
answer_d: Sense of belonging

question: Andrea and Jacinta are playing in the construction corner, competing to make the tallest tower with blocks. Andrea notices that her friend's tower is taller than hers, so she throws a block to knock it down, achieving her goal. Then, Jacinta gets angry and throws a block at her head. The educator, noticing the conflict, quickly arrives to talk to them and decides to use the pedagogical arbitration technique. Considering the previous situation and the technique referred to, what is the first step the educator should take?
answer_a: Clarify the conflict
answer_b: Suggest solutions
answer_c: Present rules
answer_d: Reconstruct the conflict

question: In relation to play as an organized physical activity, at what age does one of the essential characteristics of play correspond to individual participation rather than cooperative?
answer_a: 6 years old
answer_b: 8 years old
answer_c: 10 years old
answer_d: 12 years old

question: Which of the following authors proposes in their theory of motor development evolution, 4 phases ranging from the impulsive body to the represented body from 0 to 12 years old?
answer_a: Piaget
answer_b: Le Boulch
answer_c: Wallon
answer_d: Gallahue

question: Which of the following options corresponds to a common element in the learning theories of Piaget and Vygotsky?
answer_a: The systemic organization of children's thinking
answer_b: Language as an essential element for cognitive development
answer_c: The importance of cultural tools in development
answer_d: Dynamic positioning as a necessary requirement for learning activity

question: Considering the potential for cognitive development, what differences can be observed between Piaget's and Vygotsky's proposals?
answer_a: For Piaget, it is dependent on the stage in which the individual finds themselves; whereas for Vygotsky, it depends on the zone of proximal development
answer_b: For Piaget, it depends on the manner in which assimilation and accommodation occur; whereas for Vygotsky, it depends on how the scaffolding process is presented
answer_c: For Piaget, it depends on the different types of operations that the subject is capable of performing; whereas for Vygotsky, it will depend on the presence or absence of a tutor or guide
answer_d: For Piaget, it is dependent on how the different stages of development are overcome; whereas for Vygotsky, it will depend on how challenging the task is to solve

question: In relation to thinking styles as problem-solving processes, which of the following actions corresponds to the exercise of divergent thinking?
answer_a: Evaluate various courses of action according to a goal
answer_b: Explore unusual possibilities for response and action
answer_c: Search for a correct answer within an unknown field
answer_d: Practice a strategy to solve problems in challenging areas

question: Which of the following definitions of intelligence is most consistent with Gardner's notion of multiple intelligences?
answer_a: Intelligence is creating products that are valuable in one or more cultures
answer_b: Intelligence is demonstrating outstanding ability to solve problems
answer_c: Intelligence is the effectiveness with which people perceive and understand their own emotions and those of others
answer_d: Intelligence is the capacity for self-management for the development of personal projects in complex and challenging social contexts

question: Which of the following statements presents a valid relationship between the development of attachment and later affective bonds; according to Bowlby's theory?
answer_a: Individuals who develop attachment with a caregiver other than the biological mother are less likely to establish trusting relationships
answer_b: Individuals with caregivers who vary the intensity of attention provided during early ages show greater development of affective independence
answer_c: Individuals who have poor attachment figures in their early childhood can establish reparative relationships but tend to develop more mistrust
answer_d: Individuals who did not develop attachment in the early years of life show a greater tendency to seek support and proximity, as well as to express emotions, whether positive or negative

question: What reference is fundamental to determine mental health from a psychosocial perspective?
answer_a: The symptoms of a mental illness
answer_b: The perception of one's own efficacy in the world
answer_c: The adaptability of the individual's behavior
answer_d: The conditions and environments that shape the life experience

question:
Read the following situation:
A three-year-old boy cries when his mother does not come to pick him up at the usual time, even though the educator has told him that she called on the phone and will arrive soon.
According to the routine and daily life of the child, from which criterion would this be considered abnormal behavior?
answer_a: Evaluative
answer_b: Homeostatic
answer_c: Sociocultural
answer_d: Empirical-statistical

question: According to Kohlberg's moral development, what is a capability of people who are completing their development at the postconventional level?
answer_a: To recognize others and be able to empathize with them
answer_b: To recognize and take a stand on universal values
answer_c: To recognize the relativity of norms and choose one's own
answer_d: To recognize the existence of pre-established norms and develop the desire to follow them

question:
Read the following text:
This methodology contributed to early childhood education the pedagogical documentation, in which adults collect evidence through various forms, such as written records, photographs, and videos. The children also participate in the records, expressing their interests, conflicts, anecdotes, and a multitude of situations that can become a powerful tool for making pedagogical decisions and constitute a good strategy to enhance their identity.
Which curricular model is being alluded to in the previous text?
answer_a: Waldorf
answer_b: High Scope
answer_c: Montessori
answer_d: Reggio Emilia

question: According to Piaget, what is the significance of symbolic play in the cognitive development of a child?
answer_a: It involves, through action, developing the ability to adapt to the environment, strengthening their motor skills
answer_b: It involves, through stacking objects, the development of spatial concepts, cause and effect, and perceiving properties of objects
answer_c: It involves, through imitation, developing the ability to distinguish the imaginary from the real, consolidating their own mental representations
answer_d: It involves, through the acceptance of rules, the development of skills such as problem-solving, reasoning, and strategy analysis

question: Considering Piaget's theory, which of the following behaviors is a sign that a child is ending the sensorimotor stage?
answer_a: Pía alternately takes the pieces of a puzzle and rotates them, trying to fit them together
answer_b: Rafael takes the lid of a wooden pot that is on the floor, goes to the furniture and places it on the pot
answer_c: Andrea looks for the ball that fell under the table and looks from different sides until she finds it
answer_d: Pedro laughs every time he shakes a rattle and it sounds. When it falls and rolls, he follows it until he takes it again

question:
A preschool educator reads the story 'The Very Hungry Caterpillar' to her group of boys and girls, they discuss it, and then she suggests they make a presentation about healthy and unhealthy foods and their consequences. For this, she divides the class into two small groups: one will make a poster with healthy foods and the other, a poster with unhealthy foods. To conclude, they present together and discuss the experience.
What learning does this experience mainly promote in the children?
answer_a: Making informative posters
answer_b: Communicating their ideas and decisions to others
answer_c: Respecting the participation and contributions of others
answer_d: Identifying situations that allow for self-care

question: An educator decides to assign to the children tasks related to the care of the plants in the room. She asks them to comment on what they would like to do. The children say: “I like to draw; I will make a picture of each plant,” “I love taking care of others, at home I take care of my puppy... I will water them!” Which of the following aspects of identity development do the children demonstrate in their comments?
answer_a: Self-efficacy
answer_b: Self-concept
answer_c: Self-regulation
answer_d: Self-esteem

question: A preschool educator, in order to promote the cross-curricular learning goal: "Act with increasing independence, expanding her repertoire of actions, according to her needs and interests", asks each child to store the materials at the end of the activity in designated areas. The educator observes that Matilda stores the materials without respecting the labeling on the furniture, placing them in different places. What interaction would provide formative feedback to Matilda and contribute to achieving the proposed cross-curricular learning goal?
answer_a: "Matilda, that basket with dice and number cards doesn't go there, where do you think it might go?"; the girl looks at the labels and finds the correct place
answer_b: "Matilda, does that basket with dice and number cards go there?" The educator reminds her that she needs to look at the labels to know where each material goes; the girl observes and stores it in the correct place
answer_c: "Matilda, look at the label under the basket you just stored, does it correspond to the material you are storing?" The educator shows her where the shadow is; the girl stores the material in the indicated place
answer_d: "Matilda, I noticed you stored the materials as I requested, but what should you look at to know where they go? Next time, pay close attention to where to store them by observing how your classmates are doing it."

question: An educator will address the following learning objective in Social Interaction and Citizenship: "Show interest in interacting with boys and girls, recognizing the diversity of their characteristics." Which of the following evaluative strategies is appropriate to measure the achievement of this objective?
answer_a: Use an observation checklist while they play in the yard with children from other levels
answer_b: Apply a performance rubric while the children participate in photo exhibitions of their families
answer_c: Apply a rating scale while the boys and girls conduct an interview with people from the community
answer_d: Use pedagogical documentation while the children participate in a fair about various cultures of the country

question: A group in the senior nursery level consists of ten children. They all move around confidently and enjoy movement activities. They have started to show interest in challenges such as carrying, hiding, stacking, and combining objects. Therefore, the teacher plans to address the following learning objectives: “Experiment with objects by solving concrete situations, such as reaching for objects, pressing buttons on sound devices, taking toys out of containers, collecting objects, among others” and “Show interest and satisfaction when moving freely in daily and playful situations”. Considering the characteristics of this group of children, what learning strategy would allow the teacher to address the selected objectives?
answer_a: Heuristic play: the children explore, manipulate and combine objects, discovering the world at their own pace
answer_b: Motor circuit: the children complete a series of courses with different challenges, following a specific order
answer_c: Treasure basket: the children explore while seated around a basket filled with everyday and selected objects
answer_d: Artistic installation: the children play, move and interact with various aesthetic elements arranged in the space

question:
A kindergarten teacher for a younger middle level plans to work on the area of verbal language and also reinforce fine motor skills. To do this, she conducts the following educational experience: The children, guided by a story, pretend to be pirates searching for hidden coins in the room, which they then must put through the slot of a treasure chest. The teacher observes that Amanda kept her coins in her pocket, so the teacher asks her why she didn't put them in the treasure chest, and she replied: "I can't put the coins in because they fall." 
What intervention by the teacher would allow Amanda to receive formative feedback to achieve the learning objective?
answer_a: "Amanda, hold the coins between your fingers and I will help you insert them." Guide her hand to insert some coins. Then ask: "Can you try it by yourself?"
answer_b: "Amanda, would you like to try with another piggy bank? I have some with larger slots and that could be easier. Would you like to try again? I'll give you more time for it."
answer_c: "Amanda, do you need help? Would you like someone to show you how to insert the coins? Look at that classmate, he is doing it correctly, stand next to him so you can try it again."
answer_d: "Amanda, can you show me how you are doing it? Why do you think you can't put the coins in? Could you do it another way?" After listening to her answers, model the manipulation of the coin and practice together

question:
A teacher needs to select a technological tool that facilitates communication among the members of each group with each other and with her; allows for sharing and editing documents in real time; and can establish tasks and assign them to each member of the group.
Which of the following tools best meets the teacher's requirements?
answer_a: A virtual board for sharing links like Symbaloo
answer_b: An application for brainstorming like Stormboard
answer_c: An online data storage service like Google Drive
answer_d: A site for visually exchanging opinions like Marqueed

question: The teacher of an EMTP specialty decides to work on a learning module focused on Entrepreneurship and employability. In class, he tells the students that, gathered in groups, they must develop a proposal to create a labor union organization. He indicates that it will be a project conducted over an entire month, so they will have time to review the relevant regulations, consult workers about their experiences, and prepare a proposal suitable to the work context they choose. Considering the type of evidence the teacher will need to collect from the work done by students, what would be the most appropriate assessment tool to apply?
answer_a: Oral interview
answer_b: Checklist
answer_c: Written questionnaire
answer_d: Knowledge test

question: Read the following description:  One of his most relevant propositions in education is the theory of Mediated Learning Experience (MLE), to which human cognitive modifiability is attributed. MLE is defined as the quality of human interaction with their environment, which involves explaining cognitive processes as a byproduct of cultural transmission. From this perspective, the mediation methodology is considered to increase the subject's ability to achieve meaningful learning, understanding that through it, the subject can adapt the learning achieved in a specific context and be able to apply it to other contexts or situations, promoting the extraction of one's own experience in new learning.  Which of the following authors is the proposition about the teaching and learning process described in the previous text attributed to?
answer_a: John Dewey
answer_b: Paulo Freire
answer_c: Albert Bandura
answer_d: Reuven Feuerstein

question: A preschool educator plans to work transversally, during different moments of the daily schedule, with the following learning objective for children: "Act with progressive independence, expanding their repertoire of actions according to their needs and interests." To achieve this, she proposes to develop an active learning process through interaction with other children and adults. Which of the following learning strategies would be most appropriate to address the proposed objective?
answer_a: During recess, encourage the children to express their preferences for participating in games
answer_b: During tooth brushing times, ask the children to do it spontaneously without asking for help
answer_c: At the beginning of the day, ask the children to put on and button their aprons, providing help if necessary
answer_d: In zone play, ask the children to plan what they are going to play, the activities they will do, and with what materials

question: A preschool teacher, during zone play, notices that there is a conflict between Simón and Javiera in the construction zone. She approaches to find out what is happening and realizes that Simón is very angry because Javiera dismantled his construction and Javiera is upset because Simón took the material she was going to use. Taking advantage of this situation, the teacher decides to enhance the following cross-curricular learning objective: "Apply peaceful strategies in resolving everyday conflicts with other children."  What intervention by the teacher would be most appropriate to promote the proposed learning objective?
answer_a: Ask both what happened, how they felt, and whether their actions were peaceful or how they could be. Then, invite them to propose solutions and agreements to resolve the conflict
answer_b: Ask both what happened and comment on the importance of sharing and resolving conflicts by talking. Then, wait for them to calm down and ask them to apologize and agree on the use of materials
answer_c: Tell them that their behavior was wrong. Then, ask both how they felt about each other's reaction and invite them to resolve the conflict peacefully, by talking and sharing
answer_d: Ask both to comment on what happened individually, promoting recognition of the mistake made, and then ask them to apologize and continue working by sharing materials

question: A preschool teacher, in the area of Community and Citizenship, is developing the following learning objective: "Enjoy the closeness of children and adults in play and everyday situations."  Which behavior of the children reflects the achievement of the stated objective?
answer_a: Maximiliano sits next to Agustina when she asks him to
answer_b: Valeria greets her peers and teachers upon entering the classroom
answer_c: Rubén plays in the house area and continues playing with Renato
answer_d: Francisca shares the building blocks she is using with Pedro

question: A preschool educator in the Minor Transition level, within the Citizenship and Coexistence module, will work on the following learning objective: "Understand that some of their actions and decisions regarding the development of games and collective projects influence those of their peers." To achieve this, she invites the children to participate in a playful experience on the patio, where they will organize into teams to carry out competitive games. At the end of the experience, what intervention by the educator would promote the achievement of the learning objective?
answer_a: What were the rules of the game? What was the most difficult to comply with? Did you feel integrated by your team members?
answer_b: How did you feel about participating in the game? What did you think about the result of the competition? What would you change next time?
answer_c: What decisions did you make to organize into teams? Was there any conflict among you? If so, how did you resolve it?
answer_d: How did you contribute to the game? What would happen if you had to solve the challenges on your own? What would have happened if one of you had not participated?

question: A kindergarten teacher will share with her group a motor story to address the following learning objective from the Mathematical Thinking core: "To experiment with various objects by establishing serial relationships." Additionally, she has selected a cross-cutting learning objective from the Physicality and Movement core: "To coordinate their psychomotor skills by practicing strength and traction movements."  What learning experience would be suitable for both purposes?
answer_a: The children perform the story "Rapunzel." The characters must pass through a web of elastic bands and then decorate the protagonist's hair with bows, repeating the large-small order
answer_b: The children perform the story "The Three Little Pigs," organizing themselves into two teams. They will transport blocks in wheelbarrows to build the houses, arranging them from the smallest to the largest
answer_c: The children perform the story "Little Red Riding Hood." The characters will run along a marked path, carrying a basket full of fruits, which they will later sort by size and type
answer_d: The children perform the story "Goldilocks." First, they complete the bear family's circuit through the forest, avoiding different obstacles, and upon arriving, they organize the plates, spoons, and chairs by size, from largest to smallest

question: A Kindergarten educator, in the Natural Environment Exploration core, is conducting a gardening experience based on the following transversal learning objective from the Corporality and Movement core: "Use spatial location categories." Considering the educational level of the children, which performance most accurately reflects the achievement of the transversal objective?
answer_a: Pablo says: "Let's put a pot up on the window."
answer_b: Ignacia says: "We need to put seeds and then soil on top."
answer_c: Juan says: "Francisca, the shovels go inside the bucket, not outside."
answer_d: Fernanda says: "Let's plant these flowers between the fence and the tree."

question: Considering the development of verbal language in children, what characterizes the prelinguistic stage as opposed to the linguistic stage?
answer_a: The prelinguistic stage is characterized by the use of sounds, holophrases, and simple phrases; unlike the linguistic stage, which begins with the use of sentences
answer_b: The prelinguistic stage is characterized by the use of words, phrases, and simple sentences; unlike the linguistic stage, which involves the development of reading and writing
answer_c: The prelinguistic stage is characterized by the comprehension of language structures and the use of meaningful gestures; unlike the linguistic stage, which is distinguished by the use of the first words
answer_d: The prelinguistic stage is characterized by the use of sounds like babbling and cooing; unlike the linguistic stage, where these acquire meaning and later become the first syllables

question: In a higher middle level, a group of children is playing in the sandbox. Sara piles up sand, adds some rocks to the sides, and runs a car through it. Then she says, "I made a very big hill and the road is dangerous, just like the one near my house!"  In relation to the core of Understanding the Sociocultural Environment, which of the following learning objectives is achieved in Sara's performance?
answer_a: Recognize ways of life in the community
answer_b: Identify protection and safety norms
answer_c: Describe common activities in her community
answer_d: Distinguish elements of the natural and cultural landscape

question: An educational team at the Nursery level aims to collect evidence monthly regarding the following indicator of the Socio-Cultural Environment Understanding core: "Imitates actions of people in their close surroundings, distinguishing the actions each child performs and the use they give to everyday utensils."  What evaluation strategy would be most appropriate for the described situation?
answer_a: Use observation records during work moments in the home area
answer_b: Use an evaluation rubric during free play with the costume trunk
answer_c: Apply a checklist during the exploration of house elements in work stations
answer_d: Apply an appreciation scale while playing "Whose is it?", discovering personal items

question: A third-grade teacher, in the unit about children's rights, selected the following excerpt from the story *The Girl Who Had No Name*, by Saúl Schkolnik, to start working with his students on the right to identity:  Once upon a time, there was a girl who had no name at all. It's not that she had a really strange name, or one that was very difficult to pronounce, or one of those very, very old names, or perhaps too foreign... No! She simply had no name at all. The thing is, when one's name is Maria and someone calls: —Maria! One makes a Maria face and answers: —Who is calling me? But, if one has no name at all, then one will never be able to make the face of someone... And the features will kind of blur until one ends up like having no face.  Which of the following questions could the teacher ask to directly connect what was read with the right that will be studied in class?
answer_a: What information about the girl in the story caught your attention the most and why?
answer_b: Which part of the story do you think relates to children's rights?
answer_c: What do you think the consequences of not having a name would be for the girl in the story?
answer_d: How might the story continue to have a positive ending for the girl in the story?

question: A teacher in a 4th-year high school class conducts an evaluation to verify if his students can analyze current phenomena in politics, culture, and the arts from a philosophical perspective that is relevant to their own experience.  Which of the following performances demonstrates a greater achievement of the learning objective?
answer_a: They classify current phenomena in contemporary society into the categories of politics, culture, and art, according to a philosophical approach of their choice
answer_b: They develop a personal argument about a contemporary social problem of their choice, citing theories or philosophical concepts discussed in class
answer_c: They counter-argue a philosophical stance that is the basis of a problem in contemporary society
answer_d: They recognize the philosophical foundations that underlie a current issue of their choice, whether political, cultural, or artistic

question: A kindergarten teacher invites the children in his group to engage in an experience to start the unit 'Our Body'. To begin the activity, they will go to the playground to search for treasure with the purpose of discovering what the new unit is about. Organized into small groups supervised by an adult, they will find clues to reach the treasure, and upon discovering it, they will return to the classroom to assemble the puzzle together with the pieces they found.  Which pedagogical principles of Early Childhood Education are primarily evident in the proposed learning experience?
answer_a: Play and relationship
answer_b: Uniqueness and unity
answer_c: Meaning and activity
answer_d: Empowerment and well-being

question: A preschool educational team aims in the short term to strengthen effective communication between the establishment and families so that they are informed about the teaching-learning process of the children. Which of the following strategies is appropriate to achieve the stated objective?
answer_a: Invite families to various exhibitions and shows of the projects carried out by the children, showcasing the educational process
answer_b: Frequently provide families with evaluative reports on the children's learning, difficulties, and support needs
answer_c: Implement workshops open to the community, addressing various topics, to enhance understanding of the children's development process
answer_d: Hold regular meetings with families to timely exchange relevant information about the children's learning process

question: The substage of Primary Circular Reactions corresponds to the Sensorimotor Stage defined by Jean Piaget.  In which situation is a key manifestation of cognitive development corresponding to this substage shown?
answer_a: The child performs repetitive movements that are pleasant to him and initially involuntary, for example: constantly moving and shaking his feet
answer_b: The child performs movements that are reflexive and instinctive acts, for example: sucking the caregiver's finger as if it were a bottle, when it is nearby
answer_c: The child performs repetitive and intentional movements and, at the same time, detects or imagines where objects are when he can't see them physically, for example: going to find a rattle and moving everything necessary to find it
answer_d: The child performs intentional movements, learns how to obtain objects by manipulating them and returning them to their original place or state, for example: taking building blocks apart and then putting them back as they were

question: A preschool teacher, after a diagnostic evaluation, plans educational strategies to enable his group of boys and girls to express their emotions and feelings.  Which of the following strategies is relevant to the teacher's purpose?
answer_a: Dramatize a story and ask the boys and girls to point out the emotion that the story provokes in them
answer_b: Invite the boys and girls to recall and draw situations that have generated different emotions for them
answer_c: Play with an emotion die and ask the boys and girls to roll it and name the emotion that comes up
answer_d: Invite the boys and girls to dance, representing different emotions as they are mentioned in the song

question: In a heterogeneous Nursery level, the educator in charge will evaluate the children's learning regarding the following objective of the Identity and Autonomy core: “Express different needs or emotions (joy, fear, sadness, among others) orally and physically.” For this, various focused observation records will be used.  Which of the following performances demonstrates the achievement of this learning objective by the children?
answer_a: Rafael smiles and applauds when his mother comes to pick him up from kindergarten
answer_b: Maria flips through a magazine and, when looking at the picture of a girl, says: Sad
answer_c: Natalia notices that Gabriel laughs when she gives him a toy and says to him: Happy!
answer_d: Miguel looks at himself in the mirror and plays at making different expressions on his face: sadness, anger, disgust

question: An educational team from a Nursery Class is planning interactions that will take place during the diaper changing period in order to cater to the children's interest in participating in that moment, along with their greater bodily control. For this, they will ask the children in what positions they want to be changed, request their collaboration in dressing and undressing, and offer them some options to choose their change of clothes. Considering the previous situation, why are the interactions planned by the educational team linked to the development of coexistence and citizenship?
answer_a: Because they encourage active communication between adults and children, allowing the child to connect with their immediate environment
answer_b: Because they allow the child to strengthen the bond with adults and share by gradually taking on responsibilities
answer_c: Because they enhance the leading role of children and allow them to integrate and work collaboratively with adults
answer_d: Because they allow the child to become aware that they are a subject of rights by being heard and considered in their interests

question: A preschool teacher within the Convivencia and Citizenship core, plans for the end of March the following learning objective: "Participate in group activities and games with their peers, talking, exchanging belongings, cooperating."  Which of the following strategies directly addresses the stated objective?
answer_a: Participate in a zone play, selecting material and planning the activity to be carried out in each corner
answer_b: Participate in the game "Simon Says", listening carefully to the teacher's instructions to execute them in the shortest time possible
answer_c: Participate in the "Treasure Basket" game, freely choosing and manipulating various elements from some baskets placed in the center of the classroom
answer_d: Participate in the "Questioning Sticks" game during the daily encounter (greeting), discussing different topics, respecting turn-taking

question: A teacher of a kindergarten class has organized the classroom into play zones and has incorporated new sensory materials such as water tables, light, sand, and seeds. The children showed evident enthusiasm for playing with the new resources; however, there were conflicts between them when using them.  Considering the educational level of the children, which of the following strategies fosters harmonious coexistence among the children?
answer_a: The teacher joins the children's play by intervening in the resolution of emerging conflicts and modeling the appropriate use of the materials
answer_b: The teacher establishes a dialogue space with the children to build agreements on the use of the materials and to resolve conflicts peacefully
answer_c: The teacher establishes specific rules for the use of the new materials during playtime and constantly reminds them to promote coexistence
answer_d: The teacher sets up a rotating system by organizing the level into small play groups to prevent conflicts and promote peaceful coexistence among peers

question: A senior kindergarten teacher has addressed the following learning objective from the Core of Coexistence and Citizenship: "Recognizing correct and incorrect actions for the harmonious coexistence of the group, which are presented in different everyday situations and games". To achieve this, during dialogue spaces, they have established rules of coexistence to find solutions to various problems that arise among peers.  Which of the following performances demonstrates the achievement of the stated objective?
answer_a: During the welcoming time, the teacher asks about the rules, and Rafael says: "You have to walk inside the classroom and not run."
answer_b: During meal time, Daniela eats part of a classmate's snack, and she cries. Ignacia, upon seeing her cry, approaches the teacher and says: "My friend needs help."
answer_c: During free play time, Matías observes Alejandro who is playing with a truck, then he approaches, takes the toy and says: "It's my turn now, the teacher said we have to share."
answer_d: During work time in zones, Leonor and Sebastián throw wooden blocks from one place in the classroom to another. Agustín approaches and tells them: "You shouldn't do that, you might hit us with the blocks."

question: A teacher in a kindergarten class has decided to work with the children around the following objective from the Sociocultural Environment Understanding Core: "To understand the roles played by family and community members and their contribution to the common well-being." For this purpose, the teacher proposes that the children draw what they enjoy doing with their family and then discuss the roles each member plays in that situation. When presenting her work, Martina shows her family vacation and comments: "Here I drew when we went to the beach with my mom and grandma, here I am playing with all my cousins and my dog. We slept in a tent and had a barbecue."  Which of the following teacher interventions guides the girl towards achieving the proposed learning objective?
answer_a: Your drawing is very complete, Martina. Congratulations! Could you tell us who prepared the barbecue and who set up the tent?
answer_b: Very good, Martina! Great detail in your drawing of what you all do. What activities do you like most during your vacation?
answer_c: It is a very detailed drawing. Good job, Martina! Can you tell us what other delicious things your mom cooked? Were you able to help her?
answer_d: Excellent drawing, Martina! We can clearly see the family members. What other activities do you do during your vacations?

question: What skills are primarily developed in boys and girls through rule-based play?
answer_a: The symbolization of real situations
answer_b: Empathy and conflict resolution
answer_c: The socializing elements of agreements and taking turns
answer_d: The learning of socially established practices and roles

question: In which of the following situations is the pedagogical principle of empowerment favored?
answer_a: Experiences that respond to the interests of children and consider their previous experiences, thus supporting their learning
answer_b: Experiences that allow the child to learn to be, learn to think, and learn to act
answer_c: Experiences that consider the styles and rhythms of learning specific to each child
answer_d: Experiences that allow children to recognize their personal abilities, thus developing self-confidence to face new challenges

question: Which of the following activities promotes the development of empathy in preschool children?
answer_a: Do an artistic activity in pairs, in which both children start a drawing and then exchange it to finish it
answer_b: Ask them to develop an object in groups with waste materials, and then ask them to describe what was most difficult for them and why
answer_c: Do a role play in which the children represent a family member during a recreated lunch and point out how they felt impersonating them
answer_d: Ask the children to perform the story "The Selfish Giant," in which each child assumes the role of one of the characters in the story
